title: High Pressure, No Symptoms

patient.name: Mr Cheong Kok Wah
patient.presenting_complaint: Routine review; NCT readings are higher than normal but he has no symptoms

history.hpc: Mr Cheong attends a routine review and has NCT done. He has no eye pain, redness, or visual symptoms. He says: 'I feel completely fine, my eyes no problem one.' His NCT readings come back above the normal range in both eyes. The PSA must obtain reliable readings, repeat to confirm, and flag the elevated IOP even though he is asymptomatic.

examination_findings.fundus: Optic discs to be assessed by doctor

investigations.nct: NCT performed correctly: contact parts wiped, glasses removed, patient informed about the air puff, right eye first. Elevated readings repeated to confirm consistency. RE 26 mmHg, LE 24 mmHg — both above the normal 10-21 mmHg range. Family history of glaucoma noted.

diagnosis: Elevated IOP on NCT in an asymptomatic patient with a family history of glaucoma — a result that must still be flagged for assessment because glaucoma is often symptomless. The PSA competency is reliable NCT, confirming the elevated reading, and flagging it; diagnosis is the doctor's.

immediate: Perform NCT correctly (wipe parts, remove glasses, inform patient, right eye first)
Repeat the elevated readings to confirm they are consistent
Note the family history of glaucoma as an additional risk factor
Flag the elevated IOP for doctor review even though the patient is asymptomatic
Document the readings against the normal range and that they were confirmed
Reassure the patient and explain why further checks are needed
follow_up: Doctor to assess with Goldmann tonometry, optic disc, and visual field as indicated
Advise the patient to attend the recommended follow-up
patient_education: Explain that the eye pressure is higher than normal even though he feels fine
Explain that glaucoma often has no symptoms, so the high reading needs checking, especially with his family history
Reassure him that finding it early is exactly the benefit of the check

key_points: Elicits the family history of glaucoma
Confirms no contraindication and that glasses are removed
Performs NCT with correct hygiene, positioning, and technique
Repeats to confirm the elevated readings are consistent
Records readings against the normal 10-21 mmHg range
Recognises elevated IOP needs flagging despite no symptoms
Considers the family history as raising risk
Knows NCT alone does not diagnose glaucoma
Flags the result for doctor review and refers appropriately
Explains the result to the patient without over-stating it
